findings.title: Chunk callback reads input vectors without validity (NULL) guard
findings.description: The @njit loop indexes a_amt/a_co/a_hco/a_hr/a_rt/a_rx[i] for every row 0..n-1 without ever fetching the DuckDB validity mask (no duckdb_vector_get_validity). For a NULL input cell DuckDB does not initialize the data-slot value, so the loop reads an undefined value and folds it into the score. WHY it is wrong: this is the value-domain inverse of the carray sizing — the data buffer is allocated full-width (STANDARD_VECTOR_SIZE), so the read is in-bounds (not an OOB/use-after-free), but the byte content for a NULL row is garbage, yielding a silently wrong score. The irr.py UDAF is the in-repo reference that does this correctly (duckdb_vector_get_validity + skip, per understanding/udaf.md sec 2). Contrast also examples/online_scoring.py which has the analogous gap.
findings.impact: No memory-safety violation (in-bounds read of a full-width buffer). Latent correctness bug: any NULL in amount/country/home_country/hour/risk_tier/recent_txns produces a wrong fraud score that the cross-check (assert_results_match) would not catch because the reference path also has no NULL rows. Inert as written because setup_data generates dense random() columns with no NULLs, so neither the benchmark nor the assert ever exercises a NULL.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) document inline that the callback requires non-NULL inputs (matching the haversine caveat) and is correct only for the dense generated data, or (b) for parity with the irr.py reference, fetch each input vector's validity via duckdb_vector_get_validity and treat a NULL row as score 0 / propagate NULL. Given the example is a usage contract, an explicit comment is the minimum.

notes:
Focus items audited and found CORRECT (no defect):

1. dtype-width match (L118-124 vs L156-165 params): DOUBLE->float64, TINYINT->int8 (country/home_country/hour/risk_tier x4), INTEGER->int32 (recent_txns), output INTEGER->int32. Every carray dtype equals the DuckDB physical element width. setup_data values all fit (country/home_country 0-19, hour 0-23, risk_tier 0-4 in int8; recent_txns 0-29 in int32; amount in float64). No reinterpret/OOB/misread. This is the load-bearing per-example contract and it is upheld.

2. carray length n (L118-124): n = duckdb_data_chunk_get_size(chunk) is exactly the vector length for this chunk, and the output vector has >= n capacity, so carray((n,)) and the 0..n-1 loop are in-bounds for every column including a_out. No OOB read/write. (Caveat: this assumes FLAT vectors. duckdb_vector_get_data + flat indexing would OOB on a CONSTANT vector, e.g. a constant-folded UDF argument; here every argument is a plain column reference from a table scan so inputs are flat. A latent assumption for a copy-paste user, but not a defect for the example's fixed SQL; left out of findings as DuckDB scalar-input flattening behavior is version-dependent and not exercised here.)

3. Logical-type create/destroy ordering (L156-168): dbl_p/tin_p/int_p are all CONSUMED by duckdb_scalar_function_add_parameter/set_return_type (L159-165) BEFORE being destroyed (L166-168), and the DuckDB C API deep-copies the logical type on add_parameter/set_return_type, so freeing the source handles before duckdb_register_scalar_function (L170) is neither a use-after-free nor a leak. Each of the three handles is created once and destroyed once; int_p is reused for both the recent_txns parameter and the return type but remains a single handle freed exactly once -> no double-free.

4. Function-handle lifecycle: func_p created L154, registered L170, destroyed L173 (after register). DuckDB copies the builder into the catalog on register, so destroying the builder afterward is correct -> no leak, no use-after-free of the registered function.

5. numpy buffer .ctypes.data lifetime (L167-168, L172-173): buf / func_buf are named locals bound through the destroy call statement, so the int address from .ctypes.data points at live memory during the C call. get_unicode_data_p("fr_jit") (L155) hands set_name a char* into a temporary str, but set_name copies the name synchronously while the str is still alive -> safe. Consistent with the haversine destroy idiom.

6. NRT/meminfo balance at the @cfunc boundary: _fraud_chunk_cb signature is void(intp,intp,intp) (no NRT-tracked types), and verified in numbox lowlevel.py:48-53 that _cast_int_to_void_p is a bare inttoptr to voidptr_t; a carray over a voidptr is non-owning (no meminfo parent), so the callback creates no refcounted objects and removerefctpass strips the no-op increfs/decrefs. No leak, no double-free, refcount-neutral. The cfunc object is a module global so its .address stays valid for the connection's life.

Conclusion: no critical/high/medium MEM defect. The unit is memory-safe as written; the single finding is a low-severity latent correctness/validity gap, inert for the example's dense data.
